limitations: Requires nonnegative spectrum and exact population autocorrelations; applies to a fixed observable rather than all observables simultaneously. The generic truncated moment extremal principle is classical, and equivalent formulas in older moment or MCMC diagnostic literature remain a residual originality risk.
scientific_summary: For a positive reversible Markov chain and a fixed centered observable, the exact first two autocorrelations give sharp closed-form envelopes for every later autocorrelation and every finite-horizon sample-mean variance. They also give a sharp lower bound on long-run variance, while positive spectral variance allows arbitrarily large long-run variance at the same two lags even in finite-state irreducible chains.
